blurb: A city of scholars and manuscripts at the edge of the Sahara.

facts.t: The traveller Ibn Battuta visited Timbuktu in 1353 on his journey through the Mali Empire. Its great mosque of mud, Djinguereber, had been built about 25 years earlier.
When armed groups held the city in 2012, librarians smuggled hundreds of thousands of old manuscripts to Bamako in footlockers and rice sacks.
